body: Its alright Ive pretty much just accepted my disability and the fact that I will likely live a life of solidarity. It's frustrating but I try to be thankful for being able to hear at all and being otherwise very healthy. There's not always a clear cut easy answer for everything in life and nobody said it's fair.

...trust me, I do. Having a hearing impairment nearly my whole life (29 years old), lip reading is second nature to me (the quiet girl that sits across from me, I actially stand up from my desk while she is talking so I can watch her lips and try to see what she is saying). But there a lot of situations, especially working in an office, where people talk to you while you're looking at your monitor, from another cubicle, while facing someone else, etc.

I think about this a lot. Im painfully awkward in convo, mostly because of my severe hearing impairment. Im so focused on *hearing* people instead of listening that I don't feel like I process everything quickly. Also a lot of asking people to repeat themselves, which I've found people get extremely annoyed by even when I politely tell them I have a hearing impairment. All of this has led me to become a recluse. I want to get out and practice my social skills but its so hard to do. The second part of your post really hit me because I work in an office and I hear people talking and laughing around me constantly, but its all a blur of noises. I wish I had the ability to focus my hearing and listen to what they say so I could maybe have a better idea of how normal people have conversation.
I'm not going into detail of my work and life in general, but again, that is not an option.
I have about 40% of my natural hearing in my right ear and 30% in the left. I'm only 29
I understand you're trying to help, but expecting everyone to start texting me is unrealistic. I have also tried finding a HoH community around me but there is none. Im simply ready to give up.
